name: Act of March 2, 1889: the Crow Creek reservation (Royce 705)
citation: Act of March 2, 1889, ch. 405, 25 Stat. 888 (in force by proclamation of February 10, 1890)
promises: Section 6 set apart for the Indians receiving rations at the Crow Creek agency the townships listed by Royce, on both banks of the Missouri.

The Act of March 2, 1889 divided the Great Sioux Reservation into separate reservations; section 21 opened the rest to sale for the benefit of the Sioux, and section 19 kept in force all provisions of the 1868 treaty and the 1877 agreement not in conflict with it (Court of Claims, 105 Ct. Cl. 725).

To win Crow Creek consent, the 1889 commissioners agreed to recommend payment for the land the Act took from the Crow Creek reservation as it stood under the 1868 treaty; Congress paid $187,039, which drew interest under the Act of March 2, 1895 (105 Ct. Cl. 725).
today: In 1946 the Court of Claims held that the United States illegally charged food rations it owed the Sioux under the 1877 agreement, and certain agency costs, against the Crow Creek trust fund (case C-531 (21)), which held the $187,039 Congress paid, at interest under the Act of March 2, 1895, for the land the 1889 Act cut from the reservation. It allowed $23,347.65 (no interest allowed) but set the recoveries off against reimbursable expenditures under section 17 of the 1889 Act and dismissed all seven petitions, so nothing was paid (105 Ct. Cl. 725). The Supreme Court vacated that judgment and remanded the cases on December 16, 1946 to consider the Indian Claims Commission Act; the Court of Claims re-entered it unchanged on June 28, 1948 (112 Ct. Cl. 50), and certiorari was denied in 1949 (as cited in ICC Docket 119, 34 Ind. Cl. Comm. 230). That ruling concerns the 1877 ration duty being paid from Crow Creek's own money, not a taking of this reservation's land or a term of the 1889 Act, so it is not counted as a breach of this record.

sources.title: Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report, Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule p. 934, Crow Creek Sioux entry
Sioux Tribe of Indians v. United States, 105 Ct. Cl. 725 (1946), Nos. C-531 (18) to (24)

openQuestions: Audit 2026-11-08 (round 14): removed the court-ruling breach on 105 Ct. Cl. 725 and moved it to today. The opinion grounds the illegal charges in article 5 of the 1877 agreement (19 Stat. 254) and the trust funds of the 1895 to 1910 sale Acts; the 1889 Act appears only through section 19 and as the source of the offsets. The 1946 judgment was vacated and re-entered unchanged in 1948 (112 Ct. Cl. 50). Status lowered to no-breach-found.

Unlike the other reservations, the Crow Creek fund was itself compensation for land lost under the 1889 Act. The wrong the court found is still the use of that money for the 1877 ration duty; the payment for the land is not said to have been inadequate. The auditor judged this not a breach of this record; a reviewer may weigh it differently.

The 1889 Act itself and the land ceded under it are recorded under cession-1889-03-02-sioux (Royce 631 and 699). This Royce row is the reservation kept. It is not marked sameEventAs that record because this row is the land kept, not the land ceded.
Later reductions of this reservation by Acts of Congress after 1889 are not in Royce's schedule and are not researched here.
The ICC accounting dockets for each reservation (114 to 119) were seen in the index but not read for this record.
No Crow Creek Sioux Tribe account of the 1889 Act was found in this pass.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Sioux, Crow Creek 1889; Docket 115 (35 Ind. Cl. Comm. 194, 1974) rules on accounting exceptions only, and Docket 114 (1963) orders an accounting of 1889 Act sale funds with no liability finding; nothing new.
compensation: Congress appropriated $187,039 for the Crow Creek land lost under the 1889 Act, held at 4 percent under the Act of March 2, 1895 (105 Ct. Cl. 725).
